query: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi has high saturation magnetization but a low coercive field, and reported single-phase fcc high-entropy alloys derived from it have coercive fields no greater than 100 Oe in the reported magnetic measurements. What single intervention could overcome this coercivity limitation? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted change relative to single-phase fcc FeCoNi or a matched derivative, the relevant compositional, structural, and measurement boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing controlled Al additions to single-phase fcc FeCoNi to form coherent B2-type nanoprecipitates will increase the coercive field beyond the typical ~100 Oe limit by providing enhanced domain wall pinning.
generation.material_initial_state: A single-phase fcc FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with a coercive field ~100 Oe and high saturation magnetization.
generation.intervention: Add a small amount of Al (e.g., 5–10 at%) to FeCoNi and perform appropriate heat treatment to induce B2-ordered nanoprecipitation.
generation.conditions: Arc-melt FeCoNi with 5–10 at% Al; homogenize at ~1000–1200 °C, then anneal at ~600–800 °C to form coherent B2 nanoprecipitates in the fcc matrix.
generation.structural_mediator: Nanoscale B2-ordered Al-containing precipitates within the fcc FeCoNi matrix.
generation.mechanism: The B2 precipitates act as effective pinning centers that impede domain wall motion, thereby increasing coercive field relative to the single-phase fcc alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in coercivity to values significantly above 100 Oe, while maintaining high saturation magnetization similar to the parent FeCoNi alloy.
generation.baseline: Single-phase fcc FeCoNi or closely matched derivative of fcc FeCoNi with coercivity at or below 100 Oe.
generation.boundary: The Al content should remain within the solubility limit needed to form a fine dispersion of B2 precipitates; excessive Al or very high annealing temperatures would risk complete phase transformation or large grains that reduce coercivity again. Measurement of coercivity performed by standard hysteresis loops using VSM or similar magnetometry methods.
generation.uncertainty: The exact Al content required and the magnitude of coercivity enhancement are not firmly constrained by existing data and may vary based on processing parameters.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare multiple FeCoNiAl alloy samples with varying Al content (e.g., 3%, 5%, 7%, 10% at%) via arc melting. Homogenize at high temperature (e.g., 1100 °C) followed by an aging heat treatment at 600–800 °C to promote B2 nanoprecipitation. Compare their magnetic hysteresis loops to those of baseline single-phase fcc FeCoNi.
measurements: XRD to confirm fcc matrix and B2 precipitates
TEM or atom-probe tomography to determine nanoprecipitate size and distribution
VSM or SQUID magnetometry to measure coercivity and saturation magnetization
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the samples show no statistically significant increase in coercivity (i.e., they remain at or below ~100 Oe) despite the presence of B2 precipitates, or if no B2 precipitates form under the described conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.
